assessment_summary.cou_name: Estimate total pressure drop and branch flow split through purge Y at 20–60 CFM for fan sizing/control under lab-like isothermal conditions

evidence_keywords: Software: FUN3D v13.5 (double precision, steady solver).
Case directories, meshes, and input decks tracked in GitLab repo cfd-purge-duct (tag v0.7).
Run logs archived with FUN3D hashes and compiler flags.
Mesh study: ΔP across the Y at 30 CFM changed +3.9% (2.1M→4.7M) and +1.8% (4.7M→10.3M).
Extrapolated asymptote suggests fine-grid remaining discretization effect ≈2–3%.
Three levels: 2.1M / 4.7M / 10.3M cells.
L2 residuals <1e-5 for continuity and momentum
branch mass balance <0.2%
pressure-drop monitor flat over last 1,000 iterations.
Incompressible assumption (M < 0.12 throughout); constant properties at 295 K
Turbulence: SST k–ω with near-wall integration; cross-check with SA (baseline).
Perforated screen modeled as a porous jump (quadratic loss)
Switching to scalable wall functions (target y+ ~35) increased ΔP ~6% and muted the secondary flow
Inlet set by prescribed volumetric flow (20, 30, 45, 60 CFM cases).
Screen implemented as internal surface with K1 = 1.7e7 1/m², K2 = 3.2e3 1/m.
coefficients from vendor curve fit at Re = 3–6×10³.
±15% perturbation in K-values leads to ±6% swing in predicted ΔP
Two points available on the lab mockup
20 CFM: test ΔP = 70 Pa (±3 Pa).
30 CFM: test ΔP = 128 Pa (±5 Pa).
lab mockup with pressure taps at stations P1 (upstream) and P2 (downstream of Y), and thermal mass flowmeter on the inlet leg
lab-like, isothermal conditions
Inlet set by prescribed volumetric flow (20, 30, 45, 60 CFM cases).
Common outlet to ambient static pressure (101.3 kPa).
Geometry: Based on Purge Duct CAD Rev D.
Flow split at 30 CFM: test 60/40 (±2%). CFD = 62/38
Comparison against bench data
CFD (fine grid, SST) = 68 Pa (−2.9%).
Flow split at 30 CFM: test 60/40 (±2%). CFD = 62/38
